html:
The Tunisian Code of Personal Status is a family law issued in Tunisia on 13 August 1956, months after independence from France. It gave women more rights than any other law in the Arab world at the time.

It was the project of Habib Bourguiba, the leader of the independence movement, who soon became president. Unlike Turkey's Civil Code, it was framed as a modern reading of Islamic law rather than a break with it.

  • It banned polygamy outright.
  • Marriage needed the consent of both spouses and a minimum age.
  • Divorce went through the courts and was open to wives as well as husbands.
  • A husband could no longer end a marriage by repudiation.

Later changes added to it, such as allowing Muslim women to marry non-Muslims in 2017. Women still inherit less than men under Tunisian law, a point of fierce debate. The code is a source of national pride and has shaped women's place in Tunisia since; compare abolition of slavery in 1846.
sum: The Tunisian Code of Personal Status is a family law issued in Tunisia on 13 August 1956, months after independence from France. It gave women more rights than any other law in the Arab world at the time.
